The working file is the complete analysis; the Markdown/PDF reports are reader copies of it. Each should be read in full — this message is only a pointer, not the analysis.

In brief: the claim is **false** as stated, true only for a much narrower claim it doesn't actually make. The physical reason is that "round-trip efficiency" bundles two different processes — Carnot-unlimited sensible-heat storage (which genuinely runs ~90-99%) and Carnot-limited heat-engine reconversion back to electricity (capped at roughly 64% even under the most favorable reading of 565°C hot-side / ambient cold-side, and realistically achieving only ~35-60% in real or specified designs). 85%+ for a true electricity-in/electricity-out round trip exceeds the physical ceiling by about 21 points regardless of engineering quality. On cost, a dedicated molten-salt-plus-turbine system at 5 MWh scores at or below lithium-ion on every one of six weighted criteria (efficiency, $/usable-kWh, response time, maturity at this scale, cycle life, footprint) — a dominated comparison, not a close trade-off. Overall confidence is MEDIUM: the physical-impossibility finding alone is HIGH (rests only on the Second Law), but the magnitude-of-shortfall and cost findings rest on empirical figures that could not be independently confirmed at source despite several direct fetch attempts.
